resources.string: GT-BMS on GNU/Linux exchanges reports with the phone over your home network only, nothing goes to the internet. Open the sync, then enter the code on the computer.
Code to enter on the computer
Leave the battery to the computer
Most batteries take one connection at a time. While charging near the computer, the phone can let go of the link and take it back by itself afterwards.
Leave the link to the computer
The link is left to the computer until %1$s
The vehicle was on and still (drawing %1$.1f A for its lights and display) when you went out of range. Switch it off if you have left it.
Rings when you walk away from the vehicle while it is on and still (lights, display). Learns its own standby current.
Liquid — blue liquid, paler as it empties; it waves and leans as the phone tilts
Cells — 20 small blocks coloured from red at the bottom to green
Horizontal — a wide battery filling in the reading direction
Dial — coloured zones and a needle at the charge
The computer is not using the battery: the phone took it back.
The phone left the home Wi-Fi: it took the battery back.
Taken back by itself when the computer does not use the battery or when you leave the home Wi-Fi.
Cells, one colour — the blocks turn yellow below 50 %, orange below 25 %, red below 15 %
Home network only. On the phone that has the reports: Send. On the other: Receive, and type the code shown. Its reports become that battery\'s own record here; nothing is sent back.
Open: on the other phone press «Receive from a phone» and type the code above.
No phone found: type its address (shown under its code).
Type the address and the 6-digit code shown on the other phone.
The other phone closed after wrong codes: open it again
%1$d new reports of %2$d received (battery %3$s). Browse them from the battery chip in Reports.
